summary: Update Support macros + internal playbooks to align with new incident comms templates (Status Page Transparency Upgrades)
description:
Background
Support is updating customer-facing responses during incidents to match the new standardized incident communication templates being rolled out as part of the Status Page Transparency Upgrades initiative.

Today, our Support macros (Zendesk + Salesforce Knowledge snippets) are inconsistent across agents, sometimes over-promise timelines/SLA, and don’t map cleanly to the new incident phases (Investigating/Identified/Mitigating/Monitoring/Resolved) and component taxonomy (Hosted API vs Streaming vs Embeddings vs Reranking; per-region where applicable).

Request
1) Update/replace Support macros to align with the new incident communication templates and tone guide.
2) Update Support escalation playbook steps (internal) to align with the new Comms Lead role + approval flow for Sev0/Sev1.
3) Ensure macros include links to the status page incident and post-incident summary when available, without disclosing sensitive details (customer-specific capacity, internal hostnames, etc.).

Scope
- Zendesk macros used by Support (first-response + follow-up during ongoing incidents)
- Salesforce Knowledge article snippets (internal-only)
- Internal playbook section for “status accuracy dispute” escalations

Non-goals
- Changing the public status page copy itself (handled in Docs/DevEx + status tooling)
- Creating new incident policies (handled in PM-612 policy ticket)

Acceptance criteria
- Macros exist for each incident phase (Investigating / Identified / Mitigating / Monitoring / Resolved) and for “Status page accuracy dispute / mismatch.”
- Macros include placeholders for: incident link, affected component(s), affected region(s), customer impact, workaround (if any), next update cadence language (non-committal), and Support escalation path.
- Language is consistent with the incident templates and does NOT include:
  - Specific customer identifiers
  - Detailed infrastructure capacity constraints
  - Commitments to specific resolution times
- Sev0/Sev1 workflow note included: Support should confirm with IC/Comms Lead before sending speculative root cause statements.
- Rollout: macros enabled for Support team + short internal announcement posted in #support with a link to the updated playbook.

References
- Confluence: sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/status-page-and-comms/incident-communication-templates.json
- Confluence: sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/escalation-playbook/status-page-customer-escalation-playbook.json
- Confluence: sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process/incident-comms-roles-and-responsibilities.json
- Context tickets: SUP-28436 (disputed status accuracy), SUP-28502 (post-incident summary format), SUP-28549 (streaming disconnects not reflected)

Owner(s)
- Support Ops: Owen Phillips (implementation in tooling)
- Comms language review: Wei Chen
- CS alignment: Jasmine Liu / Rachel Kim
- Legal sensitivity check (public phrasing patterns): Michael Grant (spot-check only)

Proposed macro set (draft names)
1) INCIDENT - Investigating (Status Page)
2) INCIDENT - Identified (Status Page)
3) INCIDENT - Mitigating (Status Page)
4) INCIDENT - Monitoring (Status Page)
5) INCIDENT - Resolved (Status Page)
6) STATUS - Accuracy dispute / Customer reports impact but status page green
7) DEDICATED/PRIVATE - Incident visibility guidance (when customer asks why not listed publicly)

Notes / constraints
- Dedicated/Private: macros must be careful and may direct customers to their account team / Support for customer-specific updates; do not imply all dedicated/private events will appear on the public status page.
- Use “We’ll share another update when we have more information” rather than fixed intervals unless Comms Lead has set a cadence.
comments: 2025-11-18 (Dev Patel): Creating this as a tooling/playbook update request. We’re seeing agents freestyle incident updates; customers are quoting back inconsistent phrasing. Please prioritize before the staged rollout of new status components. The biggest pain point is “status page green but embeddings failing” type reports—need a consistent escalation macro that collects the right info + points to the new taxonomy.

2025-11-19 (Owen Phillips): Acknowledged. I’ll implement in Zendesk first (macros + tags), then mirror into the internal-only Salesforce Knowledge snippets. Can Wei Chen review the macro wording before we publish to the team?

2025-11-19 (Wei Chen): Yes. Please keep the macro text close to the incident template language: short sentences, avoid certainty early, and include what customers can do (retry guidance / fallback if applicable) only if confirmed by IC/Comms Lead.

2025-11-20 (Jasmine Liu): For CS: please add a dedicated/private note macro. We keep getting “why isn’t my incident on the public status page” questions. We need a consistent, non-defensive explanation that doesn’t leak account specifics.

2025-11-21 (Owen Phillips): Draft macros created in Zendesk sandbox. Draft list:
- INCIDENT_INVESTIGATING_V2
- INCIDENT_IDENTIFIED_V2
- INCIDENT_MITIGATING_V2
- INCIDENT_MONITORING_V2
- INCIDENT_RESOLVED_V2
- STATUS_ACCURACY_DISPUTE_V2
- DEDICATED_PRIVATE_VISIBILITY_V1
Next: review wording + add fields/placeholder instructions.

Placeholders included:
{{statuspage_incident_url}}, {{affected_component}}, {{affected_region}}, {{customer_impact}}, {{workaround_if_any}}

Also added an internal note block for agents: “If Sev0/Sev1 and root cause not confirmed, do not speculate; confirm phrasing with IC/Comms Lead in #incidents.”

2025-11-22 (Michael Grant): Quick legal/sensitivity scan: OK. Suggest one tweak: replace “we will provide updates every X minutes” with “we’ll share another update as we learn more” unless cadence is explicitly set on the status page incident. Also avoid “SLA” mentions in macros; use “availability” or “service disruption” language.

2025-11-24 (Owen Phillips): Updates applied per legal feedback. Added “next update” sentence variant:
- Default: “We’ll share another update when we have more information.”
- Optional (only if Comms Lead sets cadence): “We’ll share updates on the status page as we learn more.”

Status accuracy dispute macro now asks for:
- request_id(s)
- timestamp window + region
- endpoint route/capability (chat/streaming/embeddings/reranking)
- customer’s observed error rate / example error codes
- links to status page component the customer believes is impacted

Escalation playbook section updated to route to SRE on-call if evidence suggests mismatch; otherwise guide customer to status page and collect artifacts.

Posting internal announcement draft for #support pending Dev Patel sign-off.

2025-11-25 (Dev Patel): Approved. Please ship to production macros and post the #support announcement with links to the escalation playbook page. Also add a note to the macros that post-incident summaries may be published after resolution and we’ll link when available (no ETA).

2025-11-25 (Owen Phillips): Done.
- Zendesk macros published to production and grouped under “Incidents (Status Page v2)”.
- Salesforce internal snippets updated.
- #support announcement posted with links to the playbook + incident template references.

Resolution: Completed macro + playbook alignment. Next steps: monitor usage and collect agent feedback after first real incident using the v2 components.
resolution: Published updated incident communication macros in Zendesk and updated internal Support playbook/snippets to align with Status Page Transparency incident templates, Comms Lead workflow, and sensitivity constraints (no SLA promises, no customer-specific capacity details). Added an escalation macro for status accuracy disputes and guidance for Dedicated/Private visibility questions.
